We close the USDJPY 30 July 160 call EKO 163.50 trade idea which we opened in FX vol: Take profit on USDJPY call EKO and add further topside on 29 April at 21.6bp for a profit of 29.4bp (closing price 51bp at 162.60 spot ref; net profit USD 88.2k). Separately, the level of spot is approaching the 163 barrier on the long USDJPY topside vega position we added in FX vol roadmap: Trading the policy credibility regime (dated 25 February). The barrier runs until mid-August and means this position has negative delta, acting as an intervention risk hedge in the near-term. USDJPY has continued to rally, in contrast to persistent market expectations of government intervention, and we think the loo se fiscal and loose monetary policy stances of the Japanese government and central bank will likely continue to weigh on the yen. We remain long USDJPY through a spot trade initiated in Adding long USD carry via long USDJPY and USDCHF (dated 23 June). Oliver Brennan, FX Volatility Strategist | BNP Paribas London Branch

records.text: TRADE IDEA T R A D E I D E A 30/06/2026 1 DM rates: Adding to our short 5y5y Germany Camille de Courcel, Head of DM Rates Strategy and Economics, Europe | MAR | Anubhav Lamichhane, G10 Rates Strategist, Europe | MAR | Steven Montgomery, G10 Rates Strategist, Europe | MAR | Katherine Yoon, Europe Rates Strategist | MAR | BNP Paribas London Branch | MAR | Andrea Fioravanti, Europe Rates Strategist Sources: Bloomberg, BNP Paribas Fig. 1: Term premia derived fair value model A confluence of factors spurs sharp rates rally: The reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, a big fall in energy prices, and misreporting of central bank speakers at times despite no change in communication have collectively contributed to the rates rally of the past week. However, we would like to flag a key omission in this list, namely quarterly rebalancing flows which we think has been the most important driver. Sharp declines in equities combined with a sharp rally in DM rates, together with falling term premium, suggest to us that quarterly rebalancing flows may have kicked in early. Our US equity team has highlighted the possibility of large quarter-end rebalancing flows. Given the quarterly outperformance of US equities over fixed income, we estimate that equity selling flows could exceed USD100bn into quarter-end, to the benefit of fixed income.
